entries.claim: The inspected NewAPI source declares existing routes for login, refresh, self, user models, top-up, pricing, and session management.
The inspected NewAPI pricing model exposes model ID, input/output/cache ratios, billing mode/expression, enabled groups, endpoint types, and a pricing version.
The inspected NewAPI pricing UI derives token input price from model_ratio multiplied by two and by a selected or available group ratio, then applies output and cache multipliers.

The inspected NewAPI pricing response structure has pricing values and a pricing version but no explicit official-source URL, official verification timestamp, or field declaring that the base value is a vendor official price.

The inspected NewAPI models.dev ratio importer selects the cheapest non-zero provider price for duplicate model names, so imported base ratios are not mechanically guaranteed to be the model vendor's own official price.

Read-only requests to the deployed first-party origins on 2026-08-30 returned system name 野菜API and version v1.0.0-rc.27 from both /api/status endpoints, HTTP 404 for /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap, HTTP 401 for unauthenticated /api/user/self, and a public /api/pricing projection containing 37 models plus pricing_version a42d372ccf0b5dd13ecf71203521f9d2. This verifies current public behavior only and does not establish a deployed desktop authorization or stable desktop pricing projection.

The locally installed official @deepseek-ai/dsh package is version 0.1.0-rc.6, points to github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, and documents dsh web as the web-profile alias, but its public CLI documentation does not establish a stable user-owned Base URL field or a safe automatic-write adapter contract.

The first governed RU-003 verification run executed five scenarios successfully but the catalog scenario failed because invoking Vitest inside the mandatory read-only source sandbox attempted to create vitest.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs in the project root. After replacing that nested runner with direct Node TypeScript module execution, local execution passed all six scenarios; redispatch was then blocked because the dispatcher revalidated the completed RU-002 dependency against RU-003's intentionally superseding current UI outputs.
The current client only registers local discovery and TCP diagnostics; configuration preview has no real model selection and account readiness is compiled unavailable.

Current client code binds both in-memory and stored desktop sessions to one line ID and deletes the stored credential when another first-party line is selected; it also fixes the comparison conversion to 6.75, renders the sidebar account as a guest, and hard-disables configuration apply. The deployed NewAPI status endpoint currently returns usd_exchange_rate 1 and quota_per_unit 500000 on both lines, and its desktop-session allowlist permits the token list, create, reveal, update and delete routes needed by a native-only setup transaction.

All five adapters are gated by exact version strings before configuration. Native adapters already parse owned configuration, retain volatile rollback and perform target verification. Bundled Codex exec help does not expose the top-level approval flag.

The active client still maps global_accelerated to api.yeschoy.com, while current dirty changes span account session, server-owned billing groups, activation, native adapters, icons and package version. Hermes and OpenClaw source modules exist only in the inherited codebase and are not registered by the stripped Tauri runtime. The JavaScript updater dependency exists, but the Rust plugin, capability, public key, endpoint, install flow and branded release workflow are not active.

The 0.4.4 Codex adapter treats any nonzero full-agent subprocess outcome or any unrecognized JSONL completion as one generic tool_request_failed result, rolls back a successfully read-back configuration and deletes a newly created token. An isolated current bundled Codex 0.152.1 probe successfully reads the generated provider, command-backed auth and local model catalog and emits item.completed plus turn.completed against a deterministic Responses server, so exact-version or basic config incompatibility is not the observed cause.

The current official NewAPI GitHub HEAD 918427d8ab41f6adaa4113d0496f1f8621855b70 exposes browser login, refresh-cookie, current-user, pricing, usage-log, and top-up routes, but no /api/desktop/v1 device-authorization boundary. Its documented browser session keeps a 15-minute access token in browser memory and a rotating HttpOnly SameSite=Strict refresh cookie, so it is not a safe drop-in desktop-device credential contract.

The current official Codex configuration reference documents ~/.codex/config.toml, model_providers.<id>.base_url, responses-only wire_api, and model_providers.<id>.auth.command as a command that prints a bearer token to stdout; auth.command must not be combined with env_key, experimental_bearer_token, or requires_openai_auth.

The current official Claude Code documentation identifies ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL as the custom endpoint setting and apiKeyHelper as a dynamic script-based credential source, supporting a preview of owned settings without placing a literal API key in settings.

The current official OpenCode provider documentation defines custom providers under provider.<id>, uses @ai-sdk/openai-compatible for OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoints, accepts options.baseURL, and identifies model entries by their exact model IDs.

The current official Pi models documentation identifies ~/.pi/agent/models.json, provider baseUrl and api fields, exact model IDs, OpenAI-compatible API modes, and an apiKey value beginning with ! as a command evaluated at request time.
The inspected deployed NewAPI revision exposes public pricing with usable groups and supported endpoints; its pricing_version values are source constants, not revisions of price data.
Codex documents custom provider base_url, responses wire_api and command-backed auth, independently of desktop build numbers.

Current official documentation defines stable custom-provider and verification seams for Hermes and OpenClaw and requires signed Tauri updater artifacts. Hermes accepts OpenAI-compatible chat-completions providers in config.yaml and supports one-shot execution. OpenClaw supports custom openai-completions providers, default model selection, headless agent execution and non-literal secret references. Tauri requires updater signatures and a public key in the client; updater signing is separate from Apple or Windows platform signing.

Both compiled origins currently expose the Responses and Chat Completions routes behind authentication, return the same public gpt-5.6-sol pricing metadata, and classify gpt-5.6-sol as OpenAI Chat compatible in the Codex special billing group. Current Codex documentation specifies custom provider base_url, Responses wire protocol and command-backed bearer authentication.

RU-002 should preserve the verified RU-001 discovery experience and add a client-only account and billing shell whose sole runtime account projection is backend_upgrade_required. It must show no fabricated account, balance, usage, price, authorization, or wallet result and must make no production account request until a later frozen unit verifies the least-privilege desktop server contract.

RU-003 should add a deterministic beginner configuration-preview planner for the fixed five-tool catalog and the two product-approved line roots. It may show only evidenced target fields and derived protocol endpoints, must leave the model ID unavailable until a server catalog exists, and must block all configuration, credential, file-read, file-write, connectivity, and rollback actions until later backend, secure-helper, and exact-version evidence is frozen.

A verification-only successor release unit should preserve RU-003 product behavior and source exactly, use the corrected direct-module acceptance scenario under the mandatory read-only sandbox, retain the original failed run as historical evidence, and avoid replaying the dispatcher dependency check that compares intentionally superseded UI outputs to RU-002.

A client-only public catalog reader and tool-access preview can use bounded anonymous GETs and project no credentials or account facts. Defensive response/time/concurrency bounds are implementation limits, not claimed production capacity or service SLA. Desktop bootstrap recognition is only a contract check, never authorization.

RU-024 should supersede RU-023 as an internal functional client candidate: make the first-party desktop session line-independent, project NewAPI status USD/CNY settings, share account state across the shell, use the authenticated model list, and add one native-only setup command for Claude Desktop's Code workspace and Codex. The command reuses or creates one dedicated unrestricted tool token per target, validates the selected account model and compiled origin, writes only owned fields with transaction-scoped in-memory rollback, returns no credential or path, and retains no backup history. DSH, other tools, server code, deployment, updater, telemetry and public release remain outside the unit.

RU-028 should be broadened before freeze into one client release-candidate correction that supersedes RU-027 and owns all existing client drift. It should activate yeschoy.com and yeschoy.pro, keep api.yeschoy.com dormant until a later validation, finish server-derived billing-group selection, extend secure verified setup to Hermes and OpenClaw, and produce macOS and Windows candidate artifacts. The updater may be wired and tested only after its public key, signed artifacts and manifest endpoint exist; otherwise the candidate must show no false update-ready claim.

A client-only 0.4.5 successor should replace the fragile full-agent activation gate with deterministic Codex config readback plus an exact selected-provider model probe and desktop launch, preserve rollback for real configuration, credential, provider or launch failures, return closed actionable reason codes, and replace detailed billing tables with a transparent cache-heavy one-hundred-million-token estimate using current NewAPI rates and exchange rate.
野菜API is an official desktop client whose first priority includes account access, balance, recharge, and usage visibility.
The current phase changes only the desktop client; NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration remain unchanged.
Desktop authorization is first-party authorization by the 野菜API website, not direct third-party provider login inside the client.
The mainland-optimized and Cloudflare global-acceleration lines share the same account, API key, model availability, and pricing semantics; only the network path differs.

The default model list shows models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool; all models may be viewed with unavailable entries disabled and explained, and a removed model is never silently substituted.
The desktop client compares the official-price baseline already configured in NewAPI with the current user's NewAPI price; it must not maintain a second independent numeric official-price table.

NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions are always maintained as the corresponding vendor official price; all 野菜API discounts are layered separately through user group ratios or explicit special billing rules.

The desktop account login uses first-party device authorization: the client opens the system browser for website login and explicit device approval, polls for completion, never places passwords, cookies, API keys, or final session credentials in the URL, handles cancellation and expiry explicitly, and supports website-side device revocation.

Desktop device authorization codes are single-use and expire after 10 minutes; access tokens last one hour and refresh automatically; the remembered device session expires after 30 days of inactivity and has a 90-day absolute reauthorization limit; logout, website revocation, and refresh failure are explicit invalidation paths, while sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.

The desktop account session uses least privilege: it may read the current account profile, balance, usage, available models, and prices and manage only the current device's per-tool relay keys and logout. Password, email, payment data, recharge records, user groups, other devices, other-device key plaintext, and administrative settings remain website-only or inaccessible.

The product owner accepted the exact-version compatibility allowlist for V1: automatic configuration is enabled only for exact tool versions that passed the complete matrix, while unknown, newly released, failed, and otherwise unverified versions remain read-only until a trusted compatibility update adds them.

The product owner authorized the next client development unit for first-party website authorization, account balance and usage, recharge entry, and official-versus-actual price presentation while preserving the existing decision that NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration are not changed in the current phase.

The product owner authorized implementation to continue after RU-002 and accepted starting the next client-only one-click configuration foundation while preserving the decision not to modify NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production configuration in this phase.
The owner directs implementation in the desktop client and a concrete backend handoff for their technical colleague; do not modify server code or production configuration.

entries.claim: Owner rejects exact-version gates and asks for general client integration without adapting every ordinary app update. Existing client-only boundary remains in force.

The owner is preparing the desktop client for release. yeschoy.com and yeschoy.pro are the two usable client origins now; api.yeschoy.com remains a first-party origin that will be repaired later but cannot currently be validated. All other client work should proceed, including truthful account and price behavior, general-version one-click setup, Hermes and OpenClaw, packaging and an update delivery plan. NewAPI, Nginx, database and server code remain outside the client work.

The owner reports that Codex Desktop activation fails on both selectable lines and requires the client to fix the false all-or-nothing gate. The owner also requires pricing to become a concise, approximately one-hundred-million-token official-versus-YesChoy comparison for a cache-heavy workload instead of a detailed per-rate table.

decisions.question: What client-only successor release unit is authorized after RU-001 when the deployed NewAPI still lacks the approved desktop authorization boundary?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-002 as a successor to RU-001. Preserve the branded five-tool read-only discovery experience and add the production account and billing information architecture, complete page states, fixed display-only 1 USD = 6.75 CNY context, and an updated future NewAPI change specification. The only runtime account projection in this unit is backend_upgrade_required: it performs no account network request, stores no credential, shows no fabricated account or numeric billing value, and exposes no active recharge or authorization action until a later frozen unit verifies a deployed least-privilege /api/desktop/v1 contract.

decisions.question: How should the accepted RU-003 implementation be verified after the original frozen acceptance runner proved incompatible with mandatory read-only isolation and redispatch rechecked superseded dependency outputs?
decisions.choice: Create RU-004 as a verification-only successor to RU-003. Preserve the RU-003 product scope, source, contract, page, and blocked side-effect boundary without modification; execute the same six semantic scenarios using the corrected direct Node TypeScript module loader plus read-only source assertions; retain the original failed run as immutable historical evidence; and declare no work-package dependency because RU-004 changes no implementation and its release-unit dependency and supersession preserve the authority chain.

decisions.question: How should the client correct dual-line Codex activation failures and simplify price comparison without weakening truth or changing NewAPI?
decisions.choice: Create a client-only 0.4.5 successor. Codex activation remains transactional, but ready is established by successful owned-field readback, Codex-native configuration and credential loading, one bounded real response through the exact selected direct or loopback provider path and successful desktop launch; a complete general-purpose Codex agent turn is no longer an installation gate because unrelated plugins, tools and evolving JSONL events can create false rollback. Return distinct closed reasons for credentials, line reachability, model rejection, invalid response and launch failure. Replace per-rate tables with one cache-heavy 100 million token example consisting of 10 million new input, 80 million cache reads and 10 million output; compute official and current-account YesChoy estimates from current NewAPI pricing, billing group ratio and exchange rate, show tier ranges where required and disclose any conservative cache fallback. Advance coherently to 0.4.5 and produce a notarized macOS universal candidate plus an explicitly unsigned Windows x64 candidate. Do not modify NewAPI, Nginx, DNS, server database, production configuration, telemetry or updater activation.
decisions.decidedBy: product owner plus current client, live route and isolated Codex runtime evidence

terms.definition: 由野菜API网站授权给桌面客户端、只用于账户和客户端管理接口的凭证状态。
依据当前用户、计费分组、模型、缓存、阶梯和价格版本计算的野菜API价格。
面向用户的 API 接入入口类别，例如大陆优化或全球线路；实际端点在高级信息中可见。
请求和本地工具配置中使用的真实模型标识，不得被推荐标签取代或隐藏。
模型厂商公开价格源在指定核对时间、单位和计费条件下声明的价格。
本地配置写入、读取回验和工具所需协议的最小连通性测试均成功后的状态。

requirements.statement: The target client account flow uses first-party browser authorization and then displays account balance, usage, and recharge entry points.
acceptance: The client never asks the user to choose GitHub or LinuxDo as a desktop-specific login provider.
If the website session is absent, the website performs its normal login before authorization.
The device code is short-lived and single-use, and the client exposes waiting, approved, rejected, expired, cancelled, and network-interrupted states.
Passwords, website cookies, API keys, and final desktop session credentials never appear in an authorization URL.
The website names and revokes authorized devices, and the client obeys revocation on its next online request.
A device code expires after 10 minutes, an access token after one hour, an inactive remembered session after 30 days, and every device requires reauthorization no later than 90 days.
The issued device session contains only the approved current-account read and current-device key-management scopes.
A backend device/authorization contract is specified before this target flow is implemented.

requirements.statement: The client displays balance and usage and opens the existing first-party wallet page in the system browser for recharge during V1.
acceptance: Balance and usage identify freshness and retry state.
Recharge does not embed payment credentials or duplicate payment settlement in the client.
Password, email, payment data, recharge-record mutation, and other sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.
The external wallet destination is restricted to the configured first-party origin.

requirements.statement: Model facts have explicit owners: NewAPI live data owns current-account availability, exact IDs, the numeric official-price baseline, and actual user pricing; a versioned first-party catalog owns compatibility, recommendations, descriptions, and any price provenance metadata not yet returned by NewAPI, but never a duplicate price number.
acceptance: No client-side fuzzy match changes an exact server model ID.
A newly available model without catalog metadata remains identifiable but is not declared compatible without evidence.
The client derives both comparison values from NewAPI's pricing semantics and never embeds an independently maintained numeric official-price table.
The bundled catalog is covered by the signed client artifact and may supplement source and verification metadata until a versioned server contract supersedes it.
NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions remain vendor official prices; discounts and promotions are represented only by separately identifiable group or special billing rules.
Automatically imported aggregator or channel prices cannot overwrite an official baseline until they are verified against the corresponding vendor source.
Tiered expressions, per-request prices, media units, current-user groups, and special pricing rules are preserved rather than reduced to a universal multiplier formula.

requirements.statement: RU-002 preserves RU-001 and adds a beginner-readable account and billing shell that truthfully reports the missing desktop backend boundary without contacting account services, storing credentials, fabricating values, or enabling recharge.
acceptance: The shell exposes clear Account and Local tools destinations and preserves the complete fixed five-tool read-only scan behavior from RU-001.
The account destination states that secure website authorization requires a future server upgrade and exposes no control that pretends authorization can currently begin or complete.
Balance, today usage, month usage, model ID, official price, actual price, and recharge remain visibly unavailable instead of showing zero, sample, cached, or inferred values.
The fixed 1 USD = 6.75 CNY comparison rate is labelled display-only and not presented as a live exchange rate or a billing input.

The runtime makes no account, pricing, usage, authorization, wallet, or other network request and persists no password, website cookie, access token, refresh token, API key, account profile, or scan history.

The updated future NewAPI specification is pinned to current official GitHub evidence, distinguishes current routes from proposed /api/desktop/v1 routes, and records the deployed 404 readiness result without changing NewAPI or production infrastructure.

requirements.statement: RU-003 preserves RU-002 and adds a beginner-readable local configuration preview for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH across the mainland-optimized and global-accelerated lines without reading or changing any tool configuration, accessing a credential, contacting a server, or inventing a model ID.
acceptance: The configuration destination presents exactly Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH in stable order and lets the user choose exactly one tool for the current preview.
The line step presents exactly mainland optimized at https://yeschoy.com and global accelerated at https://api.yeschoy.com, and the selected line root remains visible in the summary.

Claude Code previews the approved root URL, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi preview the selected root with /v1, and DSH explicitly withholds a protocol endpoint and write target because its exact web-profile adapter is not verified.
The preview names only evidenced user-owned fields, exposes no literal secret or complete user path, and clearly states that it has not read an existing configuration.
Model ID remains visibly unavailable pending the first-party model catalog; the UI displays no sample model, guessed model, price, connectivity result, or supported-version claim.
The apply control remains disabled and the projection reports networkAttempted, configurationRead, configurationWritten, and credentialAccessed as false for every tool and line selection.
RU-001 local discovery and RU-002 account and billing readiness behavior remain available and unchanged, and no NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, updater, or production resource is modified.

requirements.statement: RU-007 supplies a real anonymous first-party model/group catalog and protocol-aware five-tool preview plus an implementable backend handoff while server, credential, account and configuration-write authority remain absent.
acceptance: Only explicit user action can request the three fixed GET paths on one compiled HTTPS origin; no custom URLs, redirects, auth headers, cookies, raw upstream errors, expressions or persisted metadata reach the renderer.

Public catalog facts are labelled non-user-specific; groups are independent of network lines; models retain real IDs and declared protocols while installation compatibility, group-specific stream restrictions and account authorization remain unverified.
Line changes, refreshes and unmounts invalidate prior requests and selections; malformed, partial and failed responses never fall back to sample models, default ratios or cached authentication.

Claude Code requires declared anthropic, Codex requires openai-response, OpenCode and Pi require openai for this preview profile; DSH continues to abstain. Missing declarations block the corresponding preview without claiming that a positive declaration proves real compatibility.

No balance or actual account price is fabricated. Server display exchange rate and fixed 6.75 official comparison FX are distinct. No numeric price projection or client expression execution is introduced.

Bootstrap absence, transport failure, unsupported contract and recognized contract are distinguishable; recognition cannot activate login or apply. The backend handoff includes schema, examples, actual deployed-source evidence, missing services and server-owned acceptance.
Existing candidate regression plus new contract, protocol, race/recovery, UI and handoff tests pass; current native suite compiles and runs without skipped tests.

requirements.statement: RU-024 turns the deployed NewAPI integration into one coherent internal functional client candidate with shared first-party account state, server-owned comparison conversion, authenticated models, and native-only one-click setup for Claude Desktop's Code workspace and Codex.
acceptance: Changing between mainland optimized and global accelerated never deletes or invalidates a valid desktop credential; only confirmed expiry, revocation, logout or an authenticated 401/403 clears it.
The overview, sidebar, account, model and setup destinations consume one shared account projection and cannot simultaneously label the same current session signed in and signed out.
The account model list is the selection authority for setup and prices; stale public-preview blockers and guest-only copy no longer disable an authenticated user.

The positive usd_exchange_rate from the selected NewAPI status response is displayed and used for comparable official-reference and current-account CNY prices; an absent or malformed rate makes comparison unavailable instead of falling back to 6.75.

One-click setup supports exactly Claude Desktop's Code workspace and Codex in this unit, validates one selected account model and compiled first-party line, and reports a closed success or recovery reason.

The native command reuses or creates one dedicated unrestricted NewAPI tool token for the selected target, prefixes it for relay use, never returns it to JavaScript, and deletes a newly created token if the local write cannot commit.

Claude setup changes only the owned env fields in the existing settings object; Codex setup changes only its active model/provider table and OPENAI_API_KEY. Existing unrelated fields are preserved, writes are atomic, and an in-memory transaction snapshot restores all touched files after failure without retained backup history.
DSH, OpenCode, Pi, other tool writes, NewAPI source, database schema, Nginx, DNS, deployment, telemetry, updater and public release remain outside RU-024.

requirements.statement: Generalize installed-tool eligibility across ordinary versions without weakening identity, credential, configuration or verification boundaries.
acceptance: Unknown, future and Windows four-component version strings never gate eligibility. Missing runtime is distinct from unsupported version.
Re-resolve selected identity and check required invocation capabilities before credentials. Help probes are bounded, isolated and secret-free; no model requests on scan or help.
Failed capability checks are retryable, not proof of incompatibility. Claude Desktop remains awaiting runtime verification through its existing 3P transaction.
Preserve schema parsing, unrelated configuration, readback, external-change detection and rollback. Codex JSON startup/error output alone cannot become ready.
UI displays detected version or unread version, installed/pending verification and actionable capability errors, with no forced downgrade.
Cover future versions, missing runtime, probe failure, replay, stale identity, races and recovery. No NewAPI/server mutations or universal-future-compatibility claims.

requirements.statement: Deliver one testable client-only release candidate with two currently usable first-party lines, truthful NewAPI-owned account and price data, and secure verified one-click setup for seven explicitly named tools while keeping the unavailable API origin and unproven updater inactive.
acceptance: The only selectable lines are mainland_optimized at https://yeschoy.com and global_accelerated at https://yeschoy.pro. api.yeschoy.com is neither selected nor health-claimed and cannot receive an automatic retry of a token or other mutating request.

Changing selectable lines preserves one valid first-party desktop session. Only logout, expiry, revocation or an authenticated authorization failure clears credentials; a route or network failure remains retryable.

Available model IDs, supported endpoint types, billing groups, group ratios, usd_exchange_rate and actual prices come from the current authenticated NewAPI responses. Missing or malformed data is unavailable, never compiled or invented.

The setup surface names Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex Desktop, Pi, DSH web, Hermes and OpenClaw separately, selects an unambiguous installation, shows exact model ID and billing group, and never gates an ordinary version string by allowlist.

Hermes and OpenClaw integrations preserve unrelated configuration and resolve their credential from the signed client helper or another non-literal operating-system-protected boundary. No complete API key crosses renderer IPC, appears in ordinary configuration, logs, diagnostics, process arguments or retained backup history.

Every supported target is ready only after readback and a harmless target-level request using the selected line, exact model and credential. Configuration-only, launch-only, direct relay probe, missing runtime, ambiguous installation, target timeout and failed response remain non-success states with recovery guidance.

Renderer and native tests cover sign-in projection consistency, line switching, group pricing, future versions, install ambiguity, configuration preservation, replay, concurrent change, rollback, secret absence and all seven tool identities.

The macOS universal and Windows x64 candidate build inputs use the branded icon and matching 0.4.x versions. The Windows artifact is explicitly unsigned. An updater is exposed only after a public update key, signed payloads, a versioned manifest and tamper/relaunch tests are present; otherwise settings truthfully describe it as unavailable.
No NewAPI, Nginx, DNS, database, server source, server deployment, telemetry upload, remote agent or public production-readiness claim is part of this client unit.

requirements.statement: Correct false dual-line Codex activation rollback and present a reproducible cache-heavy 100 million token official-versus-YesChoy estimate in a client-only 0.4.5 successor.
acceptance: Codex Desktop activation for either compiled line writes and reads back only the owned provider, exact model and owned catalog, validates command-backed credential loading, completes one bounded real model response through the exact selected direct Responses or loopback Chat-conversion path, and launches the selected desktop installation before returning ready.

A full general-purpose Codex agent session, unrelated plugin availability and incidental JSONL event shape are not installation gates. Real configuration, secure-storage, authentication, line, model, invalid-response and launch failures remain non-ready, restore volatile snapshots and return distinct closed reason codes without raw body, key or local path.
The loopback Codex provider supports bounded HEAD Responses and GET Models compatibility checks without exposing credentials, accepting caller-selected upstreams or listening beyond loopback.

The price panel displays one concise 100 million token cache-heavy example: 10 million new input, 80 million cache reads and 10 million output. It derives official and current-account estimates from current NewAPI billing expressions or base prices, selected billing-group ratio and positive server exchange rate.

Multiple NewAPI price tiers produce an honest min-to-max estimate rather than hidden row selection. When no separate cache-read price exists, the calculation uses the input price and says so; request-priced or unparseable models remain unavailable rather than receiving an invented estimate.

The client version advances coherently to 0.4.5. Renderer and native tests cover calculation, tier range, fallback disclosure, both Codex transports, closed failures, secret boundaries and rollback. A notarized universal macOS DMG and an explicitly unsigned Windows 10/11 x64 NSIS candidate are produced only after their applicable gates pass.

No NewAPI, Nginx, DNS, server source, server database, production deployment, telemetry or automatic-updater activation is changed. Windows behavior is claimed only from Windows runner evidence, not macOS compilation alone.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: Both Codex transports use deterministic config, credential and exact provider-path verification, expose distinct bounded failures, launch only after success and preserve secret plus rollback boundaries under replay and recovery.

The price surface renders one reproducible cache-heavy 100 million token official-versus-YesChoy estimate, honest tier ranges and cache fallback disclosure without detailed per-rate tables or invented unsupported prices.
